curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8849-1/ (scans; the tractor with its sprayer is pages 1-14, steps 1-26; pages 15-25 are the alternate model and pages 26-27 add the 8700 motor)

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the front wheels: the column drives a shaft under the bonnet through a universal joint, and two 8-tooth gears at the front of that shaft slide the rack on the tie rod, which swings both steering arms.
functions.source: book: steps 8 and 11 (column and universal joint), 12 (front axle, rack and tie rod), 13 and 17 (the circle shows the column joining the front shaft)

functions.does: The exhaust stack on the bonnet turns as the steering wheel turns: a bevel gear on the steering shaft drives a bevel gear at the foot of the stack's long upright axle.
functions.source: inferred: steps 13 and 15 put a 14-tooth bevel gear on the front shaft and on the foot of the stack's axle where they meet, and the step 17 circle shows them together; the book doesn't say whether the turning stack is meant as a feature

functions.does: The front axle rocks side to side on the steering shaft, so the front wheels can follow uneven ground.
functions.source: inferred: step 12 builds the front axle as a separate beam hung on the shaft through its middle hole; no arrow shows it rocking

functions.does: Rolling the tractor turns the power take-off shaft sticking out at the back: a 24-tooth gear on the left rear half-axle drives an 8-tooth gear on a cross shaft, whose 24-tooth gear turns a crown gear on the short shaft out the back, three times as fast as the wheels.
functions.source: book: steps 4 (rear half-axles and 24-tooth gear), 6-7 (cross shaft and crown gear)
functions.note: only the left rear wheel drives it; the right rear wheel turns freely on its own half-axle

functions.does: The handwheel on the cab's right side raises and lowers the three-point hitch and the sprayer on it: bevel gears turn an upright shaft whose 8-tooth gear drives a crown gear on the worm's cross shaft; the worm turns a 24-tooth gear on the long shaft under the tractor, and bevel gears at its back end turn the rear cross axle, which swings the two lower hitch links up.
functions.source: book: steps 7 (worm and crown gear), 9 (long shaft with 24-tooth gear and bevel), 10 (rear cross axle with bevel), 11 (lower links), 22 (handwheel and upright shaft); inferred: that the lower links turn with the rear cross axle, by the toothed half bushes beside their toggle joints, since the toggle joints themselves only have round holes there

functions.does: The sprayer hangs on the hitch's two lower links and its top link, so it stays upright as the hitch rises.
functions.note: checked with the handwheel above: the sprayer should rise level as the lower links swing up; the worm should then hold the hitch where it's left, so dragging the sprayer or a link by itself shouldn't move it

functions.does: The four wheels roll; the front wheels turn freely on their own axles.

questions.question: Do the toothed half bushes lock the hitch's lower links to the cross axle? Is the exhaust stack meant to turn as you steer? Is only the left rear wheel driven?
